newsitem.title: USA: Neostar files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Neostar files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

text.p: NeoStar Retail Group Inc, the parent company of Babbage's and Software Etc, said on Monday it had filed a voluntary petition to reorganize under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.
In a statement, the company said the petition was filed in Federal Bankruptcy Court in Dallas.
The company "elected to seek court protection in order to strengthen vendor confidence to ensure adequate inventory for the upcoming holiday selling season," the statement said.
It said it would continue to operate in the normal course of business during the bankruptcy proceeding.
The company also has received a commitment for $70 million in debtor-in-possession financing from Foothill Group Inc's Foothill Capital Corp unit and a group of lenders.
Outside director Thomas Plaskett has been named chairman of the board and will head the restructuring effort. His predecessor, James McCurry, will continue as president and chief executive.

NeoStar, a chain of consumer software specialty stores, recorded a loss of $21.5 million, or $1.44 a share, on revenues of $75.2 million in the second quarter ended Aug 28. In the same period the previous year the company reported a loss of $5.67 million, or $0.38, on revenues of $92 million.
